Driver-side support (WDDM 2.7+ on a supported GPU, Sophia's documented condition, r5) is NOT machine-verifiable through any registry/WMI route NxCore uses - the Settings app toggle state is the authoritative driver signal. Get-NxHagsCapability therefore reports the value state with an explicit Uncertain-DriverSide capability mark (SynToolkit's honesty model: missing value = 'Default, system decides' - not Off and not proof of support; wrong type/value = 'UnsupportedValue', r4) and never claims support it cannot read. SapphireOS's comment/value contradiction (HwSchMode=2 labeled 'Disable HAGS', r3) is the canonical NxVerify argument: NEXTRIX verifies the written VALUE, not a script's label. Reboot required; the 'restart pending' condition the Settings UI shows is computed from requested-vs-live state the same way SynToolkit does.

tweaks.name: Per-application GPU preference
tweaks.description: Sets a per-application GPU routing preference through the documented UserGpuPreferences mechanism.
tweaks.objective: Route a chosen application (typically a game) to a chosen adapter on hybrid/multi-GPU systems, per app, with honest single-GPU feedback.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Documented Windows mechanism: per-app GPU preferences are stored per-user in HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\DirectX\UserGpuPreferences as a value NAMED after the application's executable path, with data 'GpuPreference=<1|2>;' (1 = power saving, 2 = high performance) - the same value the Settings > Display > Graphics page writes (DirectX Developer Blog, 'Navigating the Redesigned Graphics Settings page'). APP-PARAMETERIZED BY DESIGN: the target value NAME is the app's exe path, so a declarative registry action cannot express this mechanism; a placeholder pseudo-target would be a fake registry path, so the function form (Set-NxGpuPreference -AppPath -Preference) is the only honest representation. The function validates the exe exists, then captures the original value through the standard 10-step pipeline, journals, writes and verifies - and is the reusable primitive for per-game composition (NX02-009) and any future profile workflow. On hybrid/multi-GPU systems this routes the app to the chosen adapter (topology context from NX04-008); on single-GPU systems the write is inert, so Get-NxGpuPreferenceState marks topology relevance and the entry text states plainly that it does nothing there - honesty over placebo. Restoring 'let Windows decide' is rollback's job (exact original - usually value absent), not a written 'default' placeholder NEXTRIX cannot document.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: no per-app value; Windows decides routing (hybrid systems pick per-app heuristics).
tweaks.proposedState: Per-app value 'GpuPreference=2;' (or 'GpuPreference=1;') journaled and verified for the chosen exe.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState expects the exact 'GpuPreference=<1|2>;' string for the app's value name; Get-NxGpuPreferenceState lists the entry with its parsed preference and topology relevance.

rollback.procedure: Standard journal rollback restores the exact original value (or deletes the per-app value if it never existed).

originalState.method: 10-step pipeline capture of the per-app value (kind, value, existence) before mutation.

sideEffects: Running instances of the target app keep their current adapter until relaunch; the setting is read at app start.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4301937/ (community corroboration of the UserGpuPreferences value format)

tweaks.name: Variable Refresh Rate (windowed)
tweaks.description: Enables or disables the Windows 'Variable refresh rate' optimization for windowed games through its DirectX global-settings component.
tweaks.objective: Set the VRR-for-windowed-games component with sibling components preserved, on VRR-capable displays only.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Microsoft documents the setting and its context: the 'Optimizations for windowed games' support article states the flip-model transition 'enabl[es] modern gaming features such as Auto HDR and variable refresh rate on supported displays'. The per-user representation is the INI-style string HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\DirectX\UserGpuPreferences :: DirectXUserGlobalSettings, component VRROptimizeEnable (corroborated across reference implementations: XOS composes 'SwapEffectUpgradeEnable=1; VRROptimizeEnable=0;', r1; SynToolkit models this value family with uncertainty states, r4). WHY A COMPONENT COMPOSER, NOT A DECLARATIVE ACTION: the same value hosts SwapEffectUpgradeEnable (mechanism owned by NX02-005) and a community-known AutoHDREnable component NEXTRIX never writes - a declarative whole-value write would clobber siblings and duplicate the NX02-005 target (anti-tweak-inflation gate), so Set-NxDirectXGlobalSetting performs a journaled read-modify-write of the single component (whole value captured, one component merged, every sibling preserved, whole value verified). CONFLICT NX02-005: RESOLVED BY SHARED COMPOSER. Both entries write the same multi-field REG_SZ value from different fields through the same read-modify-write composer (Set-NxDirectXGlobalSetting), which preserves sibling components; no whole-value write exists anywhere in NEXTRIX for this value, the conflict declaration has been removed on both sides, and ordering between the two entries is irrelevant. CAPABILITY HONESTY: a VRR-capable display and GPU are required; display VRR capability is not exposed through the WMI/registry routes NxCore uses, so the condition is stated here and the Settings display pages remain the authoritative capability view - the entry is CONDITIONAL (offered, never auto-applied).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default: VRROptimizeEnable component absent from DirectXUserGlobalSettings (feature off).
tweaks.proposedState: VRROptimizeEnable=<0|1> set via component composer with all sibling components preserved.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState verifies the whole composed value; the composer re-parses and reports the VRROptimizeEnable component plus every preserved sibling.

rollback.procedure: Standard journal rollback restores the exact original whole-value string (including sibling components as they were).

originalState.method: 10-step pipeline capture of the whole DirectXUserGlobalSettings value (kind, value, existence) before mutation.

sideEffects: Running games pick the change up at relaunch; VRR behavior is display/GPU-conditional (owner-verifiable, not claimed).
